questions.prompt: What does Costco charge for its hot dog and soda combo?
questions.explanation: $1.50, the same price since 1985. Costco treats it as a loss leader that gets members through the door.
questions.source: Costco food court pricing; widely reported unchanged since 1985

questions.prompt: How much did Facebook pay to acquire Instagram in 2012?
questions.explanation: About $1 billion in cash and stock. It looked expensive at the time and now looks like one of the best deals ever made.
questions.source: Facebook announcement, April 2012

questions.prompt: How many employees did Instagram have when Facebook bought it?
questions.explanation: Just 13. That works out to roughly $77 million of deal value per employee.
questions.source: Widely reported at the time of the April 2012 acquisition

questions.prompt: What share of Apple's revenue came from the iPhone in fiscal 2023?
questions.explanation: About 52%: $200.6B of $383.3B. Services, Mac, iPad and wearables together make up the other half.
questions.source: Apple FY2023 Form 10-K (net sales by category)

questions.prompt: On average, how much revenue did Apple bring in per second in fiscal 2023?
questions.explanation: About $12,000 a second. $383.3B divided by the roughly 31.5 million seconds in a year.
questions.source: Derived: Apple FY2023 Form 10-K revenue $383.285B ÷ 31,536,000 seconds

questions.prompt: What does a Costco rotisserie chicken cost?
questions.explanation: $4.99, held for years even as costs rose. Like the hot dog, it is a deliberate traffic driver placed at the back of the store.
questions.source: Costco warehouse pricing; widely reported at $4.99 since 2009

questions.prompt: What percentage of McDonald's restaurants are run by franchisees?
questions.explanation: About 95%. McDonald's earns much of its money as a landlord and royalty collector, not by flipping burgers itself.
questions.source: McDonald's Form 10-K (approximately 95% of restaurants franchised)

questions.prompt: What is the US federal corporate income tax rate?
questions.explanation: 21%, a flat rate set by the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Before 2018 the top rate was 35%.
questions.source: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, effective 2018

questions.prompt: About how many McDonald's restaurants are there in the US?
questions.explanation: Roughly 13,500, about one for every 25,000 Americans. That is still only about a third of McDonald's 40,000+ locations worldwide.
questions.source: McDonald's Form 10-K, US restaurant count (~13,500 at end of 2023)

questions.prompt: How many customers does McDonald's serve worldwide on an average day?
questions.explanation: About 69 million a day. That is roughly 1,700 customers per restaurant per day across 40,000+ locations.
questions.source: McDonald's corporate site ('approximately 69 million customers daily')

questions.prompt: How much did Google pay for YouTube in 2006?
questions.explanation: $1.65 billion in stock, when YouTube was less than two years old. YouTube now brings in tens of billions in ad revenue a year.
questions.source: Google press release, October 2006

questions.prompt: What was Amazon's IPO price per share in 1997?
questions.explanation: $18 a share. After four stock splits, one IPO share has become 240 shares, worth tens of thousands of dollars.
questions.source: Amazon IPO, May 15, 1997

questions.prompt: How many employees did WhatsApp have when Facebook bought it in 2014?
questions.explanation: About 55 people, serving 450 million monthly users. That is roughly 8 million users per employee.
questions.source: Widely reported at the February 2014 acquisition

questions.prompt: What price did Microsoft agree to pay for Activision Blizzard?
questions.explanation: $68.7 billion, the largest acquisition in video game history. Regulators reviewed it for nearly two years before it closed in 2023.
questions.source: Microsoft announcement, January 2022

questions.prompt: Walmart's annual revenue is about $650B. How much is that per day?
questions.explanation: About $1.8 billion every day. $648.1B ÷ 365 days, or roughly $20,000 every second.
questions.source: Derived: Walmart FY2024 (ended Jan 31, 2024) total revenue $648.1B ÷ 365

questions.prompt: What price is printed on a big can of AriZona Iced Tea?
questions.explanation: 99¢, printed on the can since the 1990s. The founders have refused to raise it, absorbing cost increases instead.
questions.source: AriZona Beverages; widely reported 99¢ printed price since 1992

questions.prompt: About how many different products does a typical Costco carry?
questions.explanation: About 4,000. A typical supermarket stocks tens of thousands, and Costco's narrow selection gives it huge buying power per item.
questions.source: Costco Form 10-K ('approximately 4,000 active items' per warehouse)

questions.prompt: How many Walmart stores are there in the US (not counting Sam's Club)?
questions.explanation: About 4,600. Walmart says roughly 90% of Americans live within 10 miles of one.
questions.source: Walmart Form 10-K, Walmart U.S. segment (~4,600 stores, FY2024)

questions.prompt: What percentage of Costco's total revenue comes from membership fees?
questions.explanation: Under 2%: $4.6B of $242.3B in fiscal 2023. But those fees are nearly pure profit, worth more than half of Costco's operating income.
questions.source: Costco FY2023 Form 10-K (membership fees $4,580M; total revenue $242,290M)

questions.prompt: How many gallons of gasoline does the US use per day?
questions.explanation: About 370 million gallons a day. That is roughly 1.1 gallons per American, every day.
questions.source: US EIA, 'How much gasoline does the United States consume?' (~8.8–8.9M barrels/day in 2022–2023 × 42 gallons)

questions.prompt: What did the average US wedding cost in 2023?
questions.explanation: About $35,000. The venue is usually the biggest single line item.
questions.source: The Knot 2023 Real Weddings Study

questions.prompt: What did a 30-second ad during the 2024 Super Bowl cost?
questions.explanation: About $7 million, before paying to actually make the ad. With 120M+ viewers, that is still around 6 cents per viewer.
questions.source: CBS / widely reported Super Bowl LVIII ad pricing

questions.prompt: How much did Taylor Swift's Eras Tour gross in ticket sales?
questions.explanation: About $2.08 billion over 149 shows, the first tour ever to pass $2 billion.
questions.source: Billboard Boxscore, final Eras Tour gross (December 2024)

questions.prompt: What share of Spotify's monthly users pay for Premium?
questions.explanation: About 39%: 263M subscribers out of 675M monthly users at the end of 2024. The free, ad-supported tier is the funnel into paid.
questions.source: Spotify Q4 2024 shareholder deck (675M MAU, 263M subscribers)

questions.prompt: How many weddings take place in the US each year?
questions.explanation: About 2.1 million. At ~$35,000 each, that is a $70B+ industry.
questions.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics, marriages in 2022 (2,065,905)

questions.prompt: What is the US federal minimum wage per hour?
questions.explanation: $7.25, unchanged since 2009. Most states and many cities now set a higher minimum of their own.
questions.source: Fair Labor Standards Act; US Department of Labor

questions.prompt: How many full-time employees did Apple have at the end of fiscal 2023?
questions.explanation: About 161,000. That is about $2.4 million in revenue per employee.
questions.source: Apple FY2023 Form 10-K (approximately 161,000 full-time equivalent employees)

questions.prompt: What was Apple's gross margin in fiscal 2023?
questions.explanation: 44.1%. Products ran around 36% while Services ran around 71%, which is why Apple keeps pushing subscriptions.
questions.source: Apple FY2023 Form 10-K (total gross margin percentage 44.1%)

questions.prompt: AWS is about 16% of Amazon's revenue. What share of Amazon's operating income did it produce in 2023?
questions.explanation: About 67%: $24.6B of $36.9B. The cloud business funds the much thinner-margin retail operation.
questions.source: Amazon 2023 Form 10-K segment results (AWS operating income $24.631B; total $36.852B)

questions.prompt: How many trips did Uber complete in 2023 (rides plus deliveries)?
questions.explanation: About 9.4 billion, roughly 26 million trips a day, or more than one for every person on Earth.
questions.source: Uber Q4 2023 earnings release (full-year trips 9.44 billion)

questions.prompt: What share of new US businesses fail within their first year?
questions.explanation: About 20%. Roughly half are gone by year five, so the first year is not as deadly as people think.
questions.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics establishment survival data

questions.prompt: What share of US wage and salary workers belonged to a union in 2024?
questions.explanation: 9.9%, a record low and down from about 20% in 1983. Public-sector workers unionize at more than five times the private-sector rate.
questions.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Union Members 2024 (January 2025)

questions.prompt: What is Costco's annual Gold Star (basic) membership fee in the US?
questions.explanation: $65 a year, raised from $60 in September 2024. Costco raises it only about every five or six years, and over 90% of US and Canadian members renew.
questions.source: Costco announcement, July 2024 (fee increase effective Sept 1, 2024)

questions.prompt: What share of US GDP is consumer spending?
questions.explanation: About 68%. That is why economists watch retail sales and consumer confidence so closely.
questions.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, personal consumption expenditures as a share of GDP

questions.prompt: How many pieces of mail does the US Postal Service deliver on an average day?
questions.explanation: About 318 million a day, or 116 billion a year, to more than 165 million addresses.
questions.source: USPS Postal Facts, FY2023 (116.1B mail pieces; ~318M per day)
